      Guided setup

      Retirement Benefits

      Enter CPP, OAS, and workplace pensions as monthly amounts. Harbour North now validates government-benefit ranges and repairs accidental repeated monthly-to-annual conversions.

      Plan completeness

      Missing retirement income can make projections and optimizer recommendations misleading.

      Checking plan

      How benefit amounts are handled

      • Enter CPP as the estimated monthly amount payable at age 65. Harbour North stores the annual equivalent internally and adjusts it when the optimizer tests ages 60 or 70.
      • Enter OAS as the estimated monthly amount payable at age 65. Harbour North stores the annual equivalent internally and applies the OAS deferral adjustment when testing age 70.
      • Enter workplace pensions as monthly amounts. Harbour North stores the annual equivalent internally and treats it as taxable recurring income from its selected start age through its end age.
      • All records remain visible and editable in the Financial Ledger.

      Financial ledger

      Record the complete household picture: emergency reserves, investments, property, vehicles, other assets, income, debt and spending.

      Emergency fund

      Enter the amount specifically reserved for unexpected expenses. It is included in investable assets, net worth and retirement projections.

      Do not also include this same money in a separate Cash account, or it will be counted twice.

      Net-worth assets

      Add your home, land, vehicles, recreational property, business interests and other major assets.

      Assets appear in the complete account and asset list below and are included in total net worth.

      Financial engine validation

      Retirement Optimizer

      Choose what matters most. Harbour North ranks financially viable plans according to your goal instead of simply maximizing wealth.

      Ready to analyze

      1. Choose your primary goal

      2. Target and hard limits

      Defaults to the age saved in Household.
      Hard requirement: Spending must remain funded through the planning horizon. Unfunded plans rank below every funded plan.

      Partner retirement remains locked to the saved plan unless partner optimization is explicitly enabled in Assumptions.

      3. What Harbour North tests

      • Primary retirement ages within the Assumptions search range. A target age outside that range is added automatically.
      • CPP start ages of 60, 65, and 70 with benefit adjustments.
      • OAS start ages of 65 and 70 with deferral adjustments.
      • Partner retirement age only when deliberately unlocked.

      4. How plans are ranked

      For target-date and earliest-retirement goals, ending wealth is only a tie-breaker.

      First 15 retirement withdrawal years

      How tax-bracket optimization works

      The model targets the indexed ceiling of the first federal tax bracket for each retired account owner. Available RRSP or RRIF funds may be drawn during low-income years, taxes are recalculated, required spending is funded, and after-tax excess is retained in cash. The model does not currently optimize individual capital-gain lots, pension-income splitting or explicitly calculate OAS recovery tax.

      Ask Harbour North

      Ask Harbour North

      Ask a retirement question in plain language. Harbour North will test it on a protected copy of your plan and explain the result.

      Try asking

      Common planning questions

      Private by design
      Questions are processed inside this browser. Harbour North does not send your plan to an external AI service.
      Harbour North can test retirement age, spending, inflation, returns, CPP timing, RRSP drawdown and one-time purchases.
      How answers are produced
      Calculation method and limitations

      Harbour North recognizes supported planning questions, creates a cloned scenario, runs the existing projection engine, and compares the result with the active plan. It does not use a general-purpose language model or provide regulated financial advice.

      Results depend on the data and assumptions entered. Tax, benefit, market and pension rules may change. Confirm important decisions with qualified Canadian professionals.

      Review a strategy first

      Once reviewed, you can keep the strategy as a comparison or walk through a protected, guided adoption.

      How Harbour North reaches this verdictView methodology

      The Decision Centre compares the selected strategy with the current plan using the same projection and tax engines. It considers lifetime tax, ending net worth, funding status, shortfall timing and the size of the differences.

      A favourable verdict does not mean the strategy is suitable in every real-world situation. Liquidity, tax rules, personal preferences and account restrictions should be reviewed before implementation.
